name: Peace by Committee: The Search for World Order
description: A hundred and fifty years of attempts to stop war by treaty, assembly and law, from the Red Cross to the League of Nations to the United Nations.

checkpoints.name: Rules for war
checkpoints.note: The Geneva Conventions and the Red Cross try to make war less cruel. The First World War shows how weak such rules are and convinces Woodrow Wilson that nations need a body to settle disputes.

checkpoints.name: The League tries
checkpoints.note: After the Treaty of Versailles the League of Nations is set up, and the Kellogg-Briand Pact outlaws war on paper. Neither stops aggressors, and the Munich Agreement shows the limits of appeasement.

checkpoints.name: A new start
checkpoints.note: Out of the Second World War come the United Nations and its Charter, plus the World Bank, Nuremberg trials and Bretton Woods system, built to fix the mistakes made after the first war.

checkpoints.name: Blocs and brinkmanship
checkpoints.note: The Marshall Plan, NATO and the Warsaw Pact split Europe, the UN fights in Korea and sends peacekeepers after Suez under Hammarskjöld, the WHO fights disease, and the Non-Proliferation Treaty limits atomic weapons.

checkpoints.name: A looser world
checkpoints.note: After the Berlin Wall falls the European Union, World Trade Organization and African Union gather states in new ways, and the Paris Agreement turns to a shared threat to everyone, the climate.
